says: A frame with a hit in it contains something near white.
why: Those three measure 0.949, 0.849 and 1.000. A hit is read as a flash, and a flash that is not the brightest thing on screen is not a flash. This is the one thing allowed to outshine the cat.

says: Effects take the full chroma nothing else is allowed.
why: Those measure 1.000, 0.901 and 1.000. The world sits low in saturation on purpose, so full chroma is a channel nothing else uses and an effect is separable by colour alone.

says: Effects stay sparse. The screen never becomes noise.
why: Those four run 0.009 to 0.057. Vampire Survivors measures 0.190 and is the failure this bound exists to stop: past that the frame is noise and the player cannot find their own character. It is in the shelf as the negative case and is deliberately not cited here.

says: No effect is smaller than 0.3 m across.
why: The cat is 0.8 m and about 5% of the frame, so 1% of the frame is roughly 0.16 m. On a phone about 1080 px on its short edge, a 0.3 m effect is near 20 px. Below that it is a coloured pixel nobody can identify, and it costs the same to draw.

says: An effect is recognisable in the three frames it exists for.
why: An effect lives under half a second. Anything whose shape only resolves over a longer animation is decoration the player never sees.
